cohort: 4552 singleton parturient women and their newborns treated at the Second People's Hospital of Liaocheng, China, from June 2015 to June 2017
finding: Both low and high maternal age at childbirth were associated with increased incidence of adverse pregnancy outcomes.
mod_finding: Compared to the 20-29 year old group, the youngest group had a lower cesarean section rate and a higher premature birth rate after adjusting for confounders, while older age groups (30+) had higher rates of cesarean section, premature birth, postpartum hemorrhage, and newborn transfer to NICU.
